question: Choose ALL that apply. How can the CPU performance of a program be improved?

answers.answer: Decreasing the clock cycles per instruction (CPI).
answers.feedback: Yes. CPU time = IC x CPI / clock rate, so lowering CPI reduces CPU time.

answers.answer: Decreasing the throughput of the processor.
answers.feedback: No. Lower throughput means less work per unit time - worse performance.

answers.answer: Increasing the number of clock cycles.
answers.feedback: No. More clock cycles means more time.

answers.answer: Decreasing the response time for disk access.
answers.feedback: Yes. Faster disk access lowers the program's overall execution time.
Yes. Fewer instructions means less CPU time (CPU time = IC x CPI / clock rate).
No. A lower clock rate means each second delivers fewer cycles - worse performance.

answers.answer: Decreasing the length of the clock cycle.
answers.feedback: Yes. A shorter clock cycle means a higher clock rate, which reduces CPU time.

question: A program requires 6e9 instructions to execute on a processor running at 3 GHz. Suppose 10% of the instructions execute in 2 cycles, 70% in 3 cycles, and 20% in 4 cycles, giving an execution time of 6.2 seconds. Which adjustment improves overall performance by approximately 11%?
